case_name: Satish @ Dhanna v State of Madhya Pradesh and Others
facts: Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, Indore Bench.
Stand of the present appellant was that he was juvenile when the occurrence took place. His date of birth was 12.11.1980.
Various accused persons faced trial for offence punishable under Sections 147, 148, 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the ' IPC ').
Prior to the date of occurrence the Madhya Pradesh Children Act, 1928 (in short the ' Children Act ') was in force.
The Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 (in short ' 1986 Act ') was in operation on the date of occurrence.
Subsequently, the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 (hereinafter referred to as '2000 Act') has been enacted.
issues: Whether the accused was juvenile when the occurrence took place
petitioner_arguments: Since the accused was juvenile, his trial could not have been held alongwith others
respondent_arguments: The question whether the appellant was a juvenile was never raised earlier
court_reasoning: An accused who was juvenile cannot be denied the benefit of provisions of 2000 Act
At this distant point of time to refer the appellant to the Juvenile Board would not be proper
The sentence awarded is restricted to the period already undergone
cases_cited: Dhanna v State of Madhya Pradesh
and Bhoop Ram v. State of U
